title: His father the doctor: schooling, practice and Spanish-American War
summary: Dr. Nelson studied at Straight University, taught a surgeon, served as lieutenant at San Juan Hill, and is now old and deaf.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Were there many colored doctors at the time your father started out? I wonder, where did he go to school? Do you remember anything about his? He went to Streets University.

Oh yes, I've heard of that. Yes, he went to Streets University. That's part of Dillard now, I think. And he was over here at Flint Goodies, he was on Canal Street, Canal and Robinson. I don't know if you don't remember that.
Oh I've heard of it though, I remember when it was there. It's now one up on Louisiana.
Yeah, and he taught Dr. Federicks, Rivers Federicks, that great colored surgeon area. He's dead now.
How old, when was your father born about? Do you know about?
Well, it's in 18, he's 88. So that's, it's 18, I just remember the date. The 1800s or not. Yeah. See he was the first lieutenant in the Spanish American War.
He was in that, I don't know. Oh yeah.
Fought on San Juan Hill over in Cuba. Talk to him about some of those old days too.
No, he don't hear, he don't see.
All he do is just sit over there in the room.
We wouldn't want to bother him, but he couldn't hear. It would have been nice if we had a few, ten years ago. Oh sure, oh yeah. When we used to record here.
Mm-hm, he's a 32nd degree mason too. Mm-hm. Know masonry too.
